exclude: Keys generated or controlled by one operator and merely assigned different labels
Custom cryptographic verification as a substitute for native verifier outcomes
Unpinned container tags, mutable tool aliases, or unfrozen trust roots
Post-outcome protocol, key, threshold, corpus, or metric changes
Pooling systems or attacks into one success rate without per-cell counts
Treating a valid signature, TUF target, or in-toto layout as scientific warrant
include: Only the seven Git blobs in CORPUS_MANIFEST.json
Only the exact tool commits in SOFTWARE_LOCK.json
Only native cosign, python-tuf, and in-toto verification decisions for primary system endpoints
Only public keys or OIDC identities bound before execution
Every registered adverse, failure, timeout, and undetermined outcome
withdrawal_rule: A custodian may withdraw before execution; the affected slot remains missing and execution stays blocked. Replacement requires a new identity-binding commit before outcomes.
